title: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

relationships.phenotype: NEURONOPATHY, DISTAL HEREDITARY MOTOR, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT 11

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene, which encodes alpha-II spectrin.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuronopathy-11 (HMND11) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the SPTAN1 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We identified patients with heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1, in three separate dominant hereditary motor neuropathy families via next-generation sequencing.
checks.explanation: Heterozygous SPTAN1 mutations in dominant HMN families; HMND11 label is standard nomenclature.

checks.claim: The SPTAN1 gene encodes alpha-II spectrin.
checks.evidence_quote: heterozygous nonsense mutations in the αII-spectrin gene, SPTAN1
checks.explanation: Paper identifies SPTAN1 as the alpha-II spectrin gene.

paragraphs.text: Distal hereditary motor neuropathies are a rare subgroup of inherited peripheral neuropathies characterized by length-dependent axonal degeneration of lower motor neurons without significant involvement of sensory neurons (Beijer et al., 2019). HMND11 is a juvenile-onset form caused by heterozygous nonsense mutations in SPTAN1; penetrance is variable and severity differs greatly between patients (Beijer et al., 2019).

paragraphs.text: In affected members of 3 families with dominant hereditary motor neuropathy, Beijer et al. (2019) identified heterozygous nonsense mutations in the SPTAN1 gene by next-generation sequencing. Variable penetrance was noted for the mutations in 2 of the 3 families. The mutant mRNA containing the nonsense mutations was degraded by nonsense-mediated decay, leading to reduced alpha-II spectrin protein levels in patient cells. Beijer et al. (2019) noted that dominant-negative SPTAN1 mutations had previously been described as causal in a spectrum of epilepsy phenotypes.

agent.process_note: I read all three files in full. Beijer et al. (2019) is abstract only. Ylikallio et al. (2020) and Dong et al. (2021) are title only. None of them gives specific variants (nucleotide or protein changes), patient numbers, ages, ancestry beyond 'Chinese', or detailed clinical findings, so I wrote no allelic variants. No HGNC reference data was supplied, so the intro leaves out the SPTAN1 MIM number and chromosomal location. The Ylikallio title describes sensorimotor neuropathy with a developmental disorder rather than pure motor neuropathy, so I mention it only under heterogeneity.
